## `client.runs`

Start, follow, cancel and resume runs.

### `client.runs.start`

Signature: `client.runs.start(environment: str, repository: str, *, select: Sequence[str] = (), upstream: bool = False, downstream: bool = False) -> Run`

Start a run of the deployed project version (needs `RUN`).

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | Environment name. |
| `repository` | `str` | required | Repository name. |
| `select` | `Sequence[str]` | `()` | Shell-glob patterns over dotted table names; empty runs everything. |
| `upstream` | `bool` | `False` | Add every ancestor of the matched assets. |
| `downstream` | `bool` | `False` | Add every descendant of the matched assets. |

Returns: `Run`. The queued run.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.Conflict` | If a run is already active (its id is in the message), or no run principal is bound in a protected environment. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If a pattern matches nothing. |

### `client.runs.list`

Signature: `client.runs.list(environment: str, *, repository: str | None = None, status: str | Sequence[str] | None = None, trigger: str | Sequence[str] | None = None, job: str | None = None, since: datetime | None = None, sort: str | None = None, order: str | None = None, limit: int | None = None, cursor: str | None = None) -> list[Run]`

List runs, newest first, without tasks.

The runs of one page; `list_page` also returns the cursor of the next one, and `iter` walks every page.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | Environment name. |
| `repository` | `str | None` | `None` | Only this repository's runs. |
| `status` | `str | Sequence[str] | None` | `None` | Only runs in this status or one of these (``queued``, ``running``, ``succeeded``, ``failed``, ``cancelled``). |
| `trigger` | `str | Sequence[str] | None` | `None` | Only runs started this way or one of these (``schedule``, ``api``, ``manual``, ``deploy``). |
| `job` | `str | None` | `None` | Only runs of this job. |
| `since` | `datetime | None` | `None` | Only runs created at or after this time, which needs a time zone. |
| `sort` | `str | None` | `None` | What the runs are sorted by: ``created`` (the default), ``name`` (the job's, else the repository's, in any letter case), ``status``, ``environment``, ``trigger``, ``duration`` (the longest first) or ``tasks`` (the most first); runs of one value come newest first. Send the same sort with every page. |
| `order` | `str | None` | `None` | ``asc`` or ``desc``; by default ``desc`` for ``created``, ``asc`` for the others. |
| `limit` | `int | None` | `None` | Most runs returned (1 to 200); `None` leaves it to the server (100). |
| `cursor` | `str | None` | `None` | A previous page's `next_cursor`. Send the same filters with every page. |

Returns: `list of Run`. Newest first.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `limit` is outside 1 to 200, a filter value is unknown, `since` has no time zone, or `cursor` is not one the server issued for the runs list. |

### `client.runs.list_all`

Signature: `client.runs.list_all(*, environment: str | None = None, repository: str | None = None, status: str | Sequence[str] | None = None, trigger: str | Sequence[str] | None = None, job: str | None = None, since: datetime | None = None, sort: str | None = None, order: str | None = None, limit: int | None = None, cursor: str | None = None) -> RunPage`

List one page of the runs of every environment you may read, newest first.

The environments are those where you hold `READ_ENVIRONMENT`; one where you do not is left out, so this is never refused for a missing right. The order is that of `list`, over all those environments, and each run names its `environment`. With `environment`, this is `list_page` of that environment.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str | None` | `None` | Only this environment; then a missing right or environment is refused as by `list`. |
| `repository` | `str | None` | `None` | Only this repository's runs. |
| `status` | `str | Sequence[str] | None` | `None` | Only runs in this status or one of these (``queued``, ``running``, ``succeeded``, ``failed``, ``cancelled``). |
| `trigger` | `str | Sequence[str] | None` | `None` | Only runs started this way or one of these (``schedule``, ``api``, ``manual``, ``deploy``). |
| `job` | `str | None` | `None` | Only runs of this job. |
| `since` | `datetime | None` | `None` | Only runs created at or after this time, which needs a time zone. |
| `sort` | `str | None` | `None` | What the runs are sorted by: ``created`` (the default), ``name`` (the job's, else the repository's, in any letter case), ``status``, ``environment``, ``trigger``, ``duration`` (the longest first) or ``tasks`` (the most first); runs of one value come newest first. Send the same sort with every page. |
| `order` | `str | None` | `None` | ``asc`` or ``desc``; by default ``desc`` for ``created``, ``asc`` for the others. |
| `limit` | `int | None` | `None` | Most runs returned (1 to 200); `None` leaves it to the server (100). |
| `cursor` | `str | None` | `None` | A previous page's `next_cursor` of this list. Send the same filters with every page. |

Returns: `RunPage`. The runs, and the cursor for the next page (`None` on the last).

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | With `environment`, if you may not read it. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If `environment` or `repository` does not exist; or, with a sentence saying so, if the server is older than this package and has no `GET /api/v1/runs`. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `limit` is outside 1 to 200, a filter value is unknown, `since` has no time zone, or `cursor` is not one the server issued for this list. |

### `client.runs.failed`

Signature: `client.runs.failed(*, environment: str | None = None, limit: int | None = None) -> FailedRuns`

List the jobs whose newest finished run failed, in every environment you may read.

The rule is Home's "Needs your attention": per job (or per repository, for runs of no job) the newest finished run of the last seven days, kept when it failed; a later cancelled run hides an earlier failure. Each entry names the first failed task and its failure; a run that failed without a failed task has neither, and its `error_message` says why.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str | None` | `None` | Only this environment; then a missing right or environment is refused as by `list`. |
| `limit` | `int | None` | `None` | Most entries returned (1 to 200); `None` leaves it to the server (50). |

Returns: `FailedRuns`. The entries, newest end first, and whether more were left out.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | With `environment`, if you may not read it. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If `environment` does not exist; or, with a sentence saying so, if the server is older than this package and has no `GET /api/v1/runs/failed`. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `limit` is outside 1 to 200. |

### `client.runs.task_history`

Signature: `client.runs.task_history(environment: str, job: str, task: str, *, repository: str | None = None, limit: int | None = None, cursor: str | None = None) -> TaskHistoryPage`

List the attempts of one task of one job across runs, newest first.

Each entry carries what the attempt used, so a task whose memory climbs from run to run shows up. A figure that was not measured is `None`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | Environment name. |
| `job` | `str` | required | The job's name. |
| `task` | `str` | required | The task's dotted table name. |
| `repository` | `str | None` | `None` | The repository; needed only when several repositories ran a job of this name. |
| `limit` | `int | None` | `None` | Most attempts returned (1 to 200); `None` leaves it to the server (20). |
| `cursor` | `str | None` | `None` | A previous page's `next_cursor`. |

Returns: `TaskHistoryPage`. The attempts, and the cursor for the next page (`None` on the last).

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the job or task is unknown: no deployed project declares it and no run attempted it. A declared task that has not run yet gives an empty page. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If several repositories ran the job and none was named. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `limit` is outside 1 to 200 or `cursor` is not one the server issued. |

### `client.runs.log`

Signature: `client.runs.log(environment: str, run_id: str, asset: str, offset: int | None = None) -> TaskLog`

Return a task's free-text log and attempts, all of it or from a byte offset.

To follow a log, pass the previous answer's `next_offset` as `offset`: each byte then travels once. One answer carries at most 1 MiB; `more` says whether to ask again at once.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | Environment name. |
| `run_id` | `str` | required | The run. |
| `asset` | `str` | required | The task's dotted table name. |
| `offset` | `int | None` | `None` | The byte to read from; `None` returns the whole log. |

Returns: `TaskLog`. Text, where it ends in the stored log (`next_offset`), whether more is stored, whether the task is finished and its log read to the end, and attempts.

### `client.runs.wait`

Signature: `client.runs.wait(environment: str, run_id: str, timeout: float | None = None, poll_interval: float = 1.0, max_interval: float = 5.0, on_update: Callable[[Run], None] | None = None) -> Run`

Poll a run until it finishes.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | Environment name. |
| `run_id` | `str` | required | The run. |
| `timeout` | `float | None` | `None` | Seconds to keep polling, or `None` for no limit. |
| `poll_interval` | `float` | `1.0` | First interval, doubling up to `max_interval`. |
| `max_interval` | `float` | `5.0` | Largest interval. |
| `on_update` | `Callable[[Run], None] | None` | `None` | Called with every polled state (progress display). |

Returns: `Run`. The run, once `succeeded`.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.RunFailed` | If it ends `failed` or `cancelled`. |
| `TimeoutError` | If `timeout` elapses first; the run keeps going server-side. |

## `client.workers`

The workers of this instance (admin).

### `client.workers.list`

Signature: `client.workers.list() -> list[WorkerInfo]`

List the registered workers, by id.

A worker is `alive` while its heartbeat is younger than the server's lease and `lost` after that; a lost worker's row is kept for an hour. Each entry shows the run ids of what the worker is doing (a query, a deploy, a pipeline task), never SQL, and `takes` says which work it takes: `all`, `interactive` or `pipeline` (`all` when the server is of an earlier release and sends none). `caches` has the sizes of the worker's caches, `memory` the memory it last reported.

Returns: `list of WorkerInfo`. The workers; empty when none is registered.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | Without `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT` on the instance (as `scheduler.status`). |
